rules.name: Seed Set Primitive Normalization
rules.input_form: A source claim declares FSOT core seeds and/or explicitly admitted auxiliary constants.
rules.output_form: A normalized overlay basis record with tracked symbols, source-family framing, and branch links.
preconditions: The source file has been admitted to the overlay intake manifest.
The declared seed basis or auxiliary constant set is explicitly named in the source evidence.
rules.operation: Create a basis-level overlay record before any constant, workflow, or prediction claim is promoted, while preserving source-family differences in how the basis is framed.
properties: The basis record stays overlay-scoped and is not merged into the base mathematics corpus.
The overlay preserves disagreements between source families instead of flattening them into a false consensus.
Downstream claims must point back to the normalized primitive record.
examples: Normalize the thesis four-core-seed framing {pi, e, phi, gamma} together with the mathematical-key auxiliary Catalan/G usage as overlay basis record fop-001.
counterexamples: Treating the declared basis as already-validated foundational mathematics without provenance tracking.
Collapsing distinct source-family seed framings into a single invented statement that no admitted source actually makes.
common_errors: Promoting derived constants before the basis record is normalized.
Forgetting that branch links describe supporting math routes rather than endorsement of the FSOT claim itself.

dependency_links.note: Object normalization is required before overlay primitives can be tracked.

rules.name: Zero-Free-Parameter Overlay Constraint
rules.input_form: An FSOT claim or derivation path proposes a formula, workflow, or prediction object.
rules.output_form: An overlay admissibility judgment annotated with the zero-free-parameter constraint.
preconditions: The candidate claim is tied to a normalized primitive or workflow record.
The claim exposes its parameter sources explicitly enough to audit.
rules.operation: Reject or flag any promoted overlay record that violates the declared zero-free-parameter constraint.
properties: The constraint acts as a global overlay invariant.
Parameter provenance must be auditable from source record to promoted claim.
examples: Accept a prediction whose constants are routed entirely through the declared primitive seed set and tracked layers.
counterexamples: Admitting a curve-fit constant with no provenance simply because the numeric result is close to observation.
common_errors: Confusing a symbolic placeholder with a justified zero-parameter quantity.
Treating undocumented tuning as harmless bookkeeping.

dependency_links.note: Constraint checking requires a normalized primitive basis.
The constraint is treated as an invariant over the overlay derivation.

rules.name: Scalar Engine Componentization
rules.input_form: An FSOT source expresses scalar-engine variables or intermediate symbolic components.
rules.output_form: A set of normalized overlay engine objects with tracked dependencies.
preconditions: The primitive basis has already been normalized.
The source identifies engine symbols or intermediate quantities explicitly.
rules.operation: Split scalar-engine expressions into reusable named overlay objects before any prediction record is promoted.
properties: Predictions should expose which engine components they consume.
Engine symbols remain overlay-native even when their supporting mathematics uses base branches.
examples: Normalize S, K, D_eff, and psi_con as engine objects rather than leaving them embedded in prose.
counterexamples: Using an unexplained scalar engine blob with no symbol-level provenance.
common_errors: Collapsing distinct engine symbols into a single opaque constant.
Skipping dependency annotations for intermediate quantities.

dependency_links.note: Engine components inherit provenance from the normalized primitive basis.

rules.name: Dependency Tier Audit
rules.input_form: A normalized overlay primitive, workflow, or prediction record.
rules.output_form: A claim annotated with explicit dependency tier and lineage.
preconditions: The claim already has stable source and file identifiers.
Dependency layers can be traced in the dependency map evidence.
rules.operation: Attach dependency-tier metadata so later validators can distinguish primitive, layered, engine, and downstream claims.
properties: Dependency tiers prevent downstream predictions from posing as primitive content.
Lineage remains explicit across promotions into overlay rule records.
examples: Classify a cosmology prediction as depending on layer-1 constants, scalar-engine outputs, and a formula-level transformation.
counterexamples: Publishing a promoted prediction with no statement of whether it is primitive, layered, or downstream.
common_errors: Treating every source claim as if it lived at the same derivation depth.
Dropping lineage information during rulebook promotion.

dependency_links.note: Engine componentization provides the intermediate lineage nodes needed for audit.

rules.name: Falsifiability Class Split
rules.input_form: A candidate overlay prediction with provenance and dependency-tier metadata.
rules.output_form: A prediction tagged as Category A or Category B with explicit failure semantics.
preconditions: The prediction record has a stable dependency tier.
The source identifies whether failure is engine-critical or formula-local.
rules.operation: Assign the overlay prediction to the declared falsifiability class and preserve that class through later solver use.
properties: Category A claims represent engine-critical failures.
Category B claims represent formula-level failures that may not invalidate the core engine.
examples: Classify H0 as Category A and a downstream equation-of-state forecast as Category B.
counterexamples: Treating all prediction failures as equally damaging without source-backed classification.
common_errors: Mixing engine-critical and formula-level predictions in the same failure bucket.
Dropping falsifiability metadata when exporting a prediction record.

dependency_links.note: Prediction class assignment depends on the underlying dependency tier audit.

rules.name: Observable Generation Workflow Binding
rules.input_form: A user request, anchor selection state, and report-oriented candidate generation path.
rules.output_form: A normalized overlay workflow state with request, anchor, and report objects.
preconditions: The read/write workspace source has been admitted to the overlay intake.
The request specifies observables or report objectives explicitly.
rules.operation: Bind request, anchor provenance, and report objects before any generated formula is eligible for overlay promotion.
properties: The workflow record separates generation machinery from promoted scientific claims.
Report metadata should include anchor provenance and comparative evidence hooks.
examples: Normalize a FormulaGenerationRequest plus anchor-selection metadata before ranking candidate formulas.
counterexamples: Promoting an output formula without the request and anchor context that produced it.
common_errors: Confusing workflow objects with validated prediction objects.
Dropping overlap and provenance metrics from the generated report state.

dependency_links.note: The workflow is decomposed into request, anchor, and report subobjects.

rules.name: H0 Prediction Overlay
rules.input_form: A source-backed H0 claim with explicit falsifiability class and provenance.
rules.output_form: A normalized overlay prediction record for H0.
preconditions: The claim has a declared numeric prediction.
Its falsifiability class has been assigned explicitly.
rules.operation: Promote the H0 prediction into a reusable overlay prediction object with provenance and branch links.
properties: The prediction remains overlay-scoped.
Its provenance and failure class remain attached during downstream evaluation.
examples: Normalize H0 = 68.44 km/s/Mpc as a Category A prediction record.
counterexamples: Quoting H0 numerically without its falsifiability class or source file.
common_errors: Treating the number as a base-corpus theorem instead of an overlay prediction.
Dropping the dependency on the falsifiability split.

dependency_links.note: Prediction promotion requires the falsifiability class split.

rules.output_form: A normalized overlay prediction record for Omega_Lambda.

rules.operation: Promote the Omega_Lambda prediction into a reusable overlay prediction object with provenance and branch links.
properties: The prediction remains separate from base-corpus science rules.
The record can be evaluated by later benchmark tooling without losing source lineage.

counterexamples: Treating Omega_Lambda as a bare number detached from its source evidence.

preconditions: The claim has a declared numeric prediction.
Its falsifiability class has been assigned explicitly.
rules.operation: Promote the N_eff prediction into a reusable overlay prediction object with provenance and branch links.
properties: The prediction keeps engine-critical failure semantics.
The overlay record is ready for benchmark comparison without losing provenance.

counterexamples: Storing N_eff only inside a broad falsifiability narrative with no standalone record.

rules.name: dark-energy w0 Prediction Overlay
rules.input_form: A source-backed w0 claim with explicit provenance and the falsifiability class stated in the currently admitted guide.
rules.output_form: A normalized overlay prediction record for w0 that preserves the admitted-source classification rather than an older overlay assumption.
preconditions: The claim has a declared numeric value.
The claim is explicitly classified in the admitted falsifiability source.
rules.operation: Promote the w0 claim using the falsifiability class stated in the currently admitted guide, and only downgrade it if a newer admitted source supersedes that classification.
properties: The overlay should preserve source-backed classification even when earlier overlay drafts assumed a weaker status.
Classification changes should happen only when the authoritative source set changes.
examples: Normalize dark_energy_equation_of_state_w0 = -1.030 using the Category A placement currently present in the admitted falsifiability guide.
counterexamples: Keeping w0 in Category B after the admitted guide has already placed it inside the Category A section.
common_errors: Letting an older overlay assumption override the currently admitted source.
Changing falsifiability classes without a concrete source update.

dependency_links.note: w0 promotion depends on preserving the explicit falsifiability classification found in the admitted source set.

rules.name: Executable Constant Stack Normalization
rules.input_form: A runnable FSOT engine file with explicit layer-1 and layer-2 constant definitions.
rules.output_form: A theorem-level overlay record for executable constant definitions.
preconditions: The executable source is admitted to the overlay intake.
The constant names and formulas are explicit in code rather than inferred indirectly.
rules.operation: Normalize executable constant definitions as theorem-level overlay material with file-level provenance and dependency tier metadata.
properties: The code file becomes an auditable theorem source rather than a secondary implementation note.
Layer-1 and Layer-2 records remain linked back to the primitive seed basis.
examples: Normalize ALPHA, PSI_CON, ETA_EFF, OMEGA, C_EFF, A_BLEED, A_IN, P_NEW, K, and C_COSM from fsot_compute.py.
counterexamples: Treating executable definitions as untracked implementation detail even when they are the clearest available theorem source.
common_errors: Copying theorem formulas into the overlay without file provenance.
Dropping the dependency tier that distinguishes theorem-level engine material from benchmark reports.

dependency_links.note: Executable constant normalization still inherits from the primitive seed basis.

rules.name: Domain Registry and Scalar Engine Normalization
rules.input_form: A runnable FSOT engine file with explicit scalar inputs, domain metadata, and domain-scalar evaluation paths.
rules.output_form: A theorem-level overlay record for the executable scalar engine and domain registry.
preconditions: The executable source exposes the scalar input structure and domain table explicitly.
Domain-level outputs are reproducible from the admitted file.
rules.operation: Normalize the executable scalar engine and domain registry as theorem-level overlay objects with code-backed provenance.
properties: The scalar engine remains overlay-native even when it uses familiar mathematical operators.
Domain metadata and domain_scalar outputs become reusable overlay theorem records.
examples: Normalize ScalarInput, compute_scalar, DomainConfig, DOMAINS, domain_scalar, S_COSM, and S_QUANT from fsot_compute.py.
counterexamples: Leaving the domain registry implicit in prose while the executable source already defines it concretely.
common_errors: Separating domain metadata from the scalar engine that consumes it.
Treating S_COSM or S_QUANT as detached constants with no executable lineage.

dependency_links.note: The domain registry sits on top of the executable constant stack.

rules.name: Thesis Medium and D_eff Theorem Normalization
rules.input_form: A thesis source that states the 25D medium model, D_eff assignments, and master scalar framing.
rules.output_form: A theorem-level overlay record for thesis medium and D_eff claims.
preconditions: The thesis source is admitted to the overlay intake.
The medium and D_eff claims are explicit enough to quote and audit.
rules.operation: Normalize the thesis medium story and D_eff mappings as theorem-level overlay records while preserving their theory-native status.
properties: The theorem record preserves the distinction between overlay claims and accepted base mathematics.
The normalized record can route supporting reasoning into geometry, fluid, and relativity branches without contaminating them.
examples: Normalize the 25D fluid-medium framing and D_eff domain assignment tables from FSOT_Thesis.md.
counterexamples: Treating thesis narrative claims as if they were already validated geometric theorems.
common_errors: Dropping the overlay qualifier when quoting thesis-level theorems.
Flattening D_eff assignments into bare labels with no source lineage.

dependency_links.note: Executable engine normalization provides the sharper machine-facing counterpart to thesis-level scalar claims.

rules.name: Thesis Translation Registry Normalization
rules.input_form: A thesis source that enumerates translation tiers, registry counts, and correction-pipeline claims.
rules.output_form: A theorem-level overlay registry record with explicit provenance and audit scope.
preconditions: The thesis source states translation-tier or correction-pipeline claims explicitly.
The normalization pass can separate scorecard metadata from theorem content.
rules.operation: Normalize the thesis translation registry, tier definitions, and correction-pipeline claims as theorem-level overlay metadata.
properties: Registry-level claims remain auditable without pretending they are base-corpus mathematical theorems.
Correction-pipeline claims become machine-addressable for later comparative evaluation.
examples: Normalize the EXACT/NEAR/CLOSE/APPROX tier framing and correction-pipeline narrative from FSOT_Thesis.md.
counterexamples: Collapsing registry scorecards into a generic note with no theorem or provenance structure.
common_errors: Confusing translation coverage counts with proof of correctness.
Omitting the distinction between theorem records and benchmark scorekeeping records.

dependency_links.note: Translation-registry normalization builds on the broader thesis theorem frame.

rules.name: H0 Benchmark Report Promotion
rules.input_form: A concrete H0 read/write report with ranked generated candidates and target comparison metrics.
rules.output_form: A benchmark-report prediction record for the best generated H0 candidate.
preconditions: The report includes generated candidates with explicit rank, formula, and error metrics.
The promoted record remains classified as benchmark evidence rather than theorem-level validation.
rules.operation: Promote the best generated H0 candidate from the concrete report into a benchmark-report prediction record with formula, rank, score, and target comparison.
properties: The promoted record preserves report provenance and ranking metadata.
The benchmark record remains distinct from engine-critical predictions sourced from the falsifiability guide.
examples: Promote 10 * (1 + abs(p_base) * a_in / abs(c_cosm)) with computed value 67.27021167735879 and relative error 0.192564276915754 from hubble_report.json.
counterexamples: Replacing the core H0 prediction record with a generated benchmark candidate because its local error is smaller.
common_errors: Dropping the rank or score from the promoted record.
Escalating a benchmark report candidate into engine-core status.

dependency_links.note: Benchmark promotion depends on the workflow binding that preserves request, anchor, and report structure.

rules.name: Airfoil Benchmark Report Promotion
rules.input_form: A concrete airfoil dataset report with held-out metrics and promoted sandbox winners.
rules.output_form: A benchmark-report prediction record for the airfoil benchmark winner.
preconditions: The report exposes held-out train/test metrics for the promoted formula.
The promoted record remains benchmark evidence rather than theorem-level validation.
rules.operation: Promote the best held-out airfoil report candidate into a benchmark-report prediction record with formula and generalization metrics.
properties: The benchmark record stores held-out RMSE and R² rather than pretending to be a closed-form physical theorem.
The record remains tied to the concrete report file that produced it.
examples: Promote the sandbox combinatorial-search winner with held-out test RMSE 6.247387360026391 from airfoil_three_seed_report.json.
counterexamples: Treating an aeroacoustic dataset score as if it were a proven theorem about fluid mechanics.
common_errors: Quoting only the formula and omitting held-out metrics.
Comparing the record to engine-core cosmology predictions as though the evidence class were the same.

dependency_links.note: Report promotion depends on retaining the reasoning-path and report structure.

rules.name: Chemistry Benchmark Report Promotion
rules.input_form: A concrete physical-chemistry dataset report with held-out metrics and promoted sandbox winners.
rules.output_form: A benchmark-report prediction record for the chemistry benchmark winner.
preconditions: The report exposes held-out train/test metrics for the promoted formula.
The benchmark winner is distinguished from the theorem-level chemistry claims.

rules.name: Overlay Benchmark Transition Capture
rules.input_form: A benchmark report candidate plus its report provenance, falsifiability tag, and dependency tier.
rules.output_form: A provenance-rich overlay transition object that captures how benchmark evidence becomes a formal intake record.
preconditions: The benchmark candidate has a concrete report file, metric, and ranking.
The transition can preserve falsifiability and dependency-tier metadata explicitly.
rules.operation: Capture benchmark-to-overlay promotion as a dedicated overlay transition with provenance, benchmark context, dependency tier, and falsifiability metadata.
properties: The transition object records how evidence moved from raw report output into the formal overlay intake.
The same mechanism can later separate benchmark artifacts from theorem-level promotions.
examples: Capture the promotion of the generated H0 report candidate into benchmark record fpr-006 with rank, formula, score, and benchmark_report falsifiability class.
counterexamples: Adding a benchmark prediction record with no machine-readable transition metadata about how it was promoted.
common_errors: Dropping source_ids, file_ids, or intake_record_ids during promotion.
Losing the distinction between benchmark_report and engine_core falsifiability classes.

dependency_links.note: Transition capture depends on structured workflow objects and report provenance.
